the-song-of-achilles-deep-dive-character: Achilles's mother is Thetis, an immortal sea nymph, and his father is Peleus, the mortal king of Phthia.

Achilles is the son of Peleus and Thetis. Peleus is the son of Aeacus and Endeïs, and Aeacus is a son of Zeus and Aegina. Thetis is the daughter of Nereus and Doris. Achilles and Deidameia are the parents of Pyrrhus (Neoptolemus), and Achilles's cousin is Ajax, son of Telamon.
Patroclus's father is Menoetius, king of Opus, who sends him into exile; Peleus then raises him alongside Achilles.
Who is Deidameia in The Song of Achilles?
Deidameia is the princess of Scyros, daughter of King Lycomedes. Thetis hides Achilles at her father's court and arranges their marriage, and Deidameia bears Achilles's son Pyrrhus.
Who is Pyrrhus in The Song of Achilles?
Pyrrhus, also called Neoptolemus, is the son of Achilles and Deidameia. Raised by Thetis, he arrives at Troy after his father's death and is crueller than Achilles ever was.
Is The Song of Achilles based on The Iliad?
Yes. It retells events from Homer's Iliad but begins with Patroclus and Achilles's childhood and continues past the end of the Iliad, narrated by Patroclus.
Is The Song of Achilles appropriate for a 14 year old?
It is generally considered suitable for mature readers aged 14 and up. It includes battle violence, death and some intimate moments, none of them explicit.
